description: We are an AI-driven software, materials, and management team building NASA-ready prototypes—join us to design, analyze, or pitch!
summary: On long missions, astronauts carry much of the responsibility for spotting health changes in themselves, while help from Earth can be minutes away. SpaceMoni is a working web prototype of the "semi-autonomous monitoring dashboard" that NASA's Human Research Program lists as a deliverable (HRP Risk Approach Plans, EIHSO-202). One login gives each role its own view: the astronaut gets a one-line status, a clickable body map and daily self-checks; the commander gets a crew × body-system risk view and station task board; a NASA flight surgeon gets a fleet case queue. Live NOAA GOES and NASA DONKI space-weather data drive a two-stage solar-particle alert (WATCH → SHELTER). Real Inspiration4 astronaut blood data from NASA OSDR (OSD-569, OSD-575) give a reference. An Earth-delay badge shows which actions the crew can take alone and which must wait for the ground. Every number is labeled LIVE, SOURCED-STATIC, SIMULATION, ASSUMPTION or SELF-REPORTED, and a /science page maps each feature to its HRP risk and NASA-STD-3001 requirement. Prototype only, not a medical device.
details:
What it does: Astronaut home shows out-of-band readings with personal baseline and trend, self-logging of glucose, temperature, BP and HR (SELF-REPORTED), daily measurement prompts, EVA/DCS/illness log, sleep debt with Mars sol clock and PVT, mood/team check-in, SANS eye self-check, and post-landing readiness. Commander sees a crew × system risk heatmap, station objectives and workload, SPE alert and Earth-independence panel. NASA HQ/flight surgeon sees four habitats with communication delay, fleet readiness, Station objectives board with behind-schedule and over-allocation flags, and a case queue. AURA is decision support for the Crew Medical Officer: every recommendation cites NASA-STD-3001 or HRP and ends with "confirm with CMO/flight surgeon"; it never diagnoses, and falls back to an offline rules engine when the link is down.

How it works: React + TypeScript + Vite front end; serverless API on Vercel fetches NOAA SWPC GOES protons/X-ray/Kp and NASA DONKI (CME, SEP, GST, notifications) via api.nasa.gov; Inspiration4 CBC/CMP values bundled from NASA OSDR OSD-569/OSD-575 with lab reference ranges; unit tests cover delay model, SPE staging, baselines and traceability.

Why it matters: NASA's Moon to Mars Human Health and Performance white paper says crews will need to monitor their own health in real time and use decision support tools to reduce cognitive burden; SpaceMoni is an open, working sketch of that.

Honest limitations: in-mission crew vitals are SIMULATION; Inspiration4 data are pre/post-flight ground samples; Moon Base is hypothetical; this is a research demo, not a medical device.

Team: Ting-Chun Hung (CEO & CTO), Kuan-Lun Ting (Product Manager), Ssu-Ting Liao (Data Scientist). Code: https://github.com/jeffhong824/space_moni
